note: RAIA's national AI opportunity portfolio, as published. Each pillar states what exists today and what still needs to be built. That second list is unusual and valuable: it is the responsible institution stating on the record what is absent, which is the strongest available corroboration for an indicator scored zero.

nationalGoals.name: AI-enabled development
nationalGoals.detail: AI in health, education, agriculture and other sectors

anchoring: AI sits inside Vision 2050 and NST2. It is national policy rather than a standalone programme.

sectorLadder.note: RAIA's four-stage sector progression. Health is named as the working proof; agriculture, education and energy & climate are the sectors to replicate it in.

sectors.detail: The working model: consolidated, interoperable sector data feeding a live intelligence layer
Named for replication of the health model
Education named for replication of the health model
Energy and climate named for replication of the health model

pillars.name: Governance
pillars.strapline: RAIA, the national AI delivery engine
exists: RAIA established as a dedicated institution
A national AI agenda embedded in Vision 2050 and NST2
Government actively investing in AI infrastructure and institutional capability
needs: Deep institutional and programme-delivery capacity inside RAIA
Coordination mechanisms across ministries, sectors and development partners
Investment facilitation capability
Sustained international partnerships

pillars.name: Policy & Responsible AI
pillars.strapline: The trust layer: assurance, testing, cybersecurity
exists: Rwanda's data protection and cybersecurity legal framework
RAIA's governance mandate covering responsible AI
Responsible AI positioned as a design principle rather than an afterthought
needs: Model assurance and AI testing and evaluation capability: tools and institutions that verify AI systems before and during deployment
Practical, sector-usable responsible-AI rules and guidance
Cybersecurity capability scaled to an AI-enabled government
Institutional capacity to operate all of the above continuously

pillars.name: Compute
exists: Data-centre infrastructure in operation and expanding
Cloud infrastructure serving government and enterprise workloads
Growing compute demand from government use cases, universities and startups
needs: Expanded sovereign GPU capacity with high utilisation discipline
Compute-access programmes for startups, universities and government teams
Commercial AI compute facilities and cloud services
Financing and offtake structures that make compute investment bankable

pillars.name: Data
pillars.strapline: AI-ready datasets and Kinyarwanda AI data
exists: Health as the working model: consolidated, interoperable sector data feeding a live intelligence layer
Near-universal digital ID providing the identity rail for trusted data services
Government datasets across sectors at varying maturity, awaiting transformation into AI-ready form
needs: The National Data Hub itself: discovery, access and responsible-reuse infrastructure
Sector data exchanges replicating the health model in agriculture, education and energy
Systematic dataset digitisation, documentation and AI-readiness pipelines
Kinyarwanda text and speech corpora at model-training quality and scale
Data governance capability across institutions

pillars.name: Platforms & Intelligence
pillars.strapline: Shared intelligence platforms for every sector
exists: Health's intelligence layer as the working demonstration
Consolidated data environments emerging under the national data agenda
Government demand: every sector specifies an intelligence layer as stage 3 of its journey
needs: Replication of the health intelligence model in agriculture, education and energy & climate
Shared platform services: analytics infrastructure, model hosting and deployment, decision-support tooling
A national intelligence capability aggregating across sector layers
Platform operating models: who runs shared platforms and how sectors and private innovators access them

pillars.name: Financing & Partnerships
pillars.strapline: From pilot to scale: capital for every layer
exists: A national portfolio of 30+ AI use cases generating a deal pipeline
Government acting as an active market participant
Development partners and philanthropies already engaged
needs: The outcome-based fund: capitalisation, governance and payment-verification machinery
Blended-finance structures matching capital to the right layers of the stack
Co-investment vehicles and PPP frameworks for AI infrastructure
Scale-up capital pathways for solutions that have proven out

pillars.name: Skills & Delivery
pillars.strapline: 1 Million Coders and an AI-ready public workforce
exists: More than 134,000 government officials trained in AI
More than 50,000 STEM graduates in 2024
Universities and training providers active across the ecosystem
A young, growing, increasingly AI-ready workforce
needs: Coding and AI training programmes at national scale
Apprenticeship pipelines connecting training to employment
Deep technical tracks from developer training through to research and PhD programmes
Continuous reskilling as AI reshapes public- and private-sector roles

pillars.name: Innovation & Research
exists: Universities and research institutions active in the AI ecosystem
A startup community building on Rwanda's digital rails
Government-driven use cases creating applied-research problems with real deployment paths
RAIA's mandate covering research and talent
needs: Funded research programmes and AI labs with critical mass
Commercialisation pathways from university research to companies and products
Startup financing across stages
Innovation hubs connecting researchers, founders, government and capital

record.description: Every AI use case running in Rwanda. Each entry reviewed against primary documentation and dated.
record.retrievalNote: Entries transcribed from the published record on 17 September 2026 and reconciled against this platform's own registry. 42 of 43 institutions were captured. Replace with a machine-readable export when one is available, scripts/ingest_raia_record.py accepts it directly.
record.overlapNote: Only three entries are common to both registers. The two use almost entirely different names for Rwandan AI deployments, and cover different ground: the national record is public-sector weighted and current, this platform's earlier register carried private-sector and historical deployments.
